Property & Land Law Practice Guide

Land Boundary Conflicts and Encroachment Remedies in Nepal

📅 Published: 2025-05-10
🔄 Updated: 2025-10-01
⏱ 8 min read
🔍 Review: Senior Advocate Lead Counsel, Supreme Court Bar Association
Direct Legal Answer & Overview

When an adjoining landowner encroaches upon your land or disputes boundary demarcation in Nepal, three legal avenues exist: 1) Request an official cadastral re-survey and field measurement from the local Survey Office (Napi Karyalaya); 2) Lodge a formal encroachment complaint before the Municipal Ward Judicial Committee (Nyarik Samiti) under the Local Government Operation Act 2074; or 3) File an unlawful possession and boundary restoration suit (Jagga Khichola / Thamikna Mudda) in District Court under the Muluki Civil Procedure Code 2074.

Key Practical Takeaways

  • Survey Office cadastral maps (Blue Prints) take legal precedence over informal boundary markers.
  • Municipal Judicial Committees hold statutory authority to mediate minor boundary disputes.
  • District Courts can issue mandatory injunctions ordering the demolition of encroaching structures.

Rapid urbanization across Kathmandu Valley, Sunsari, and Terai cities has led to soaring land prices—and an explosion of boundary encroachment disputes. A neighbor shifting a boundary pillar by six inches or constructing an eave overhang across your property line directly infringes your constitutional right to property.

1. Step 1: The Official Napi Field Inspection

Never engage in physical confrontations. The first legal step is submitting a formal application to the local Survey Office (Napi Karyalaya) for boundary verification (Sandh Sima Chhutyaune). The official surveyor brings the permanent cadastral field book and brass measuring chains to establish the exact scientific boundary pillars based on permanent survey reference points.

2. Step 2: The Municipal Judicial Committee (Nyarik Samiti)

Under Section 47(1) of the Local Government Operation Act 2074, the Municipal Judicial Committee—chaired by the Deputy Mayor—possesses statutory jurisdiction to resolve minor boundary disputes, unauthorized eaves, and easement conflicts. The committee conducts an on-site inspection, summons both neighbors, and attempts mediated reconciliation (Milapatra).

3. Step 3: District Court Lawsuit for Encroachment (Jagga Khichola)

If the neighbor refuses to comply with survey findings, you can institute a formal lawsuit in District Court for wrongful possession and boundary restoration (Jagga Khichola Meti Thamikna Mudda). The court can issue an interim injunction restraining construction and a final mandatory injunction commanding the demolition of encroaching walls with police assistance.

Statutory Citations & Governing Nepal Legislation

Statute / Act Section / Rule Legal Significance
Local Government Operation Act 2074 Section 47(1) Empowers Municipal Judicial Committees to adjudicate and mediate land boundary conflicts.
Muluki Civil Code 2074 Part 4 (Easement and Boundary Rights) Rules on right-of-way, boundary walls, and water drainage easements.

Documentary Checklist for this Procedure

  • ✔ Lalpurja copy of the aggrieved plot and encroaching plot
  • ✔ Survey Office cadastral trace map and field book records
  • ✔ Photographs of encroaching structures or boundary fences

Frequently Asked Questions on this Topic

Can a neighbor acquire ownership of my land by long-term encroachment in Nepal?

No. Unlike some common law jurisdictions with adverse possession doctrines, Section 308 of the Muluki Civil Code 2074 strictly prohibits adverse possession against registered landowners in Nepal. Mere passage of time never turns unlawful encroachment into lawful ownership.
